source_exclusions.reason: manually reviewed one-source-frame robot insert that creates a two-project-frame flash before the intended wide action shot

reviewed_music_events.role: first lift: move from the established mechanical threat into the human team's response
commitment: reveal the operator and the machine or weapon the team has prepared
climax drive: begin the strongest sustained battle and complete its visual peak before frame 388
release: cut away from action on the stronger closing bar to a held empty aftermath

story_brief: Recut one continuous source into a chronological action trailer. Begin on the mechanical threat at the tower, move forward in source time into the workshop team's hands and device, reveal its operator, build into the strongest battle during frames 263..388, then move forward again to a held empty industrial aftermath during the musical decay. Every repeated use of Tears of Steel must advance in source time; never reuse a later image as the opening or return to an earlier source moment for the ending. The five shots must read as cause and effect: threat, preparation, reveal, battle, aftermath. The fourth shot must carry the climax and the fifth must release it; do not place fighting, firing, collision, people inspecting their arms, or major robot movement under the final decay. Every hard cut must have clean incoming handles. The reviewed musical events are editorial targets, not interchangeable metronome ticks. There is no second source quota and no parallel-world conceit.
